title: Author Correction Selective manipulation of the inositol metabolic pathway for induction of salt-tolerance in indica ric

predicted_errors.error_location: Throughout the manuscript; especially figures labelled Figure 0 through Figure 26 and the Figure 3 caption placement
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The document contains numerous embedded figures labelled Figure 0 through Figure 26, while the text only cites Figures 1–5 and supplementary figures. The Figure 3 caption (“Comparative phenotypic study...”) appears after Figure 26 rather than with its image, and “Figure 0” is nonstandard. Several of the embedded figures appear unrelated to the rice salt-tolerance study, indicating severe figure numbering, placement, and integrity errors.

After growing T3 plants under salt stress, the authors state: “Three best performing lines from each type of transgenic systems ... were selected for checking stress sustenance. Selected lines remained healthy ... while rest of the lines showed noticeable dechlorophyllisation under 300 mM stress.” Selecting lines based on the same phenotype used to assess stress tolerance is circular and biases all subsequent transcript/protein/metabolite and recovery analyses; a full or randomly chosen line set would be required for unbiased validation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Test of allergenicity for candidate protein(s), PcIMT1 results
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text reports “110 amino acids match with an allergen Solenopsis invicta of 346 amino acids” and “137 amino acids with an allergen Cupressus sempervire of 367 amino acids,” then states these correspond to matches of only 25.5% and 24.8%. If the matched lengths are 110 and 137 amino acids, the implied identities are 110/346 = 31.8% and 137/367 = 37.3%. No alternative denominator is given, so the reported percentages are inconsistent with the stated match lengths.

predicted_errors.error_location: Transcript analysis section and later T4 plant gene-expression section
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text twice uses the phrase “37-amino acid specific PcINO1-transcript” and “PcINO1 specific 37-amino acid gene transcript level expression.” A transcript is a nucleic acid and cannot be described as “37-amino acid”; this appears to confuse a protein/peptide feature with an RNA transcript and is scientifically incoherent as written.

predicted_errors.error_location: Construction of expression vectors and transcript analysis
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Methods describe construction of “pCAMBIA1301-PcINO1/OsINO1” and Results mention “accumulated INO1 transcript of OsINO1/PcINO1,” but the abstract and the rest of the paper describe only PcINO1 and PcIMT1. OsINO1 is never defined as a second transgene, endogenous control, or variant, creating an unresolved inconsistency about what was actually introduced and expressed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Abstract claim about PcINO1 line tolerance
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract states that “PcINO1 transformed transgenic rice lines exhibit significantly higher tolerance upto 200 mM or higher salt concentration with negligible compromise in their growth...” However, the Results indicate that only the three best-performing PcINO1 lines were selected and “the rest of the lines showed noticeable dechlorophyllisation under 300 mM stress.” The class-wide abstract claim therefore overstates the evidence, which is based on selected best-performing lines rather than the whole PcINO1 transgenic population.
